content:
Hi Palomar maintainers — could someone please take a look at PalomarSubmission issue 104?

My Kinin submission passed verification, but the accepted-source rendering workflow fails because it derives an exact Verso tag from Lean v4.32.2. Verso has v4.32.0 for this release line, but no v4.32.2 tag. The report classifies this as palomar.toolchain_release_missing, so there doesn't appear to be a repository-side workaround.

Failed run: https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/actions/runs/32346617765

Could you advise on a workaround or update the renderer's Lean-to-Verso compatibility handling? Thanks!

Thanks for the report!

@Kim Morrison What do you think we should do here? I'm guessing Verso isn't planning on putting out patch releases unless Verso itself needs the fix.

I can make a change where we fall back to an earlier tag of a dependency like Verso (on the same release line, so 4.32.0 in this case). That should work fine in all cases, but it does affect Palomar's claims about matching the toolchain "exactly".
This is gonna be pretty common, so we probably need to do something here

Fixed now in PalomarSubmission #113 (https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/pull/113). For a stable Lean patch release, the renderer first tries the exact Verso tag and, if that tag doesn’t exist, falls back to patch zero with the same major.minor version number. For example, Lean v4.32.2 uses Verso v4.32.0. The render report still records the exact Verso commit.
